title: Revelation 7 — The sealing of the servants: 144,000 + the great multitude

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: meta touto eidon ... hestōtas epi tas tessaras gōnias tēs gēs, kratountas ... hina mē pneē anemos. Literal and exact; Enochic cosmography correctly kept as background only.

anabainonta apo anatolēs hēliou 'ascending from the rising of the sun'; sphragida theou zōntos 'the seal of the living God'; resumptive hois ... autois correctly noted as unreproducible. theos 'God' per overlay and chapters 1, 4, 6.

citations: LWTE ch. 2 (FR 'les esclaves de notre Dieu'; EN 'the servants of our God')
verdicts.reasoning: achri sphragisōmen tous doulous tou theou hēmōn epi tōn metōpōn 'until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads' is exact. 'servants' (God as master) is the standard rendering and agrees with the canon's English edition; the French 'esclaves' is recorded. Reception note verified against LWTE-2:156-158 and confined to the labelled paragraph; no leakage.

hekaton tesserakonta tessares chiliades, esphragismenoi ek pasēs phylēs huiōn Israēl. 'sons of Israel' keeps huioi; standard English 'Israel' per the Greek-NT names convention (Hebrew-scoped shivtei-yisrael entry correctly left as background).
Iouda, Rhoubēn, Gad, each dōdeka chiliades; esphragismenoi rendered 'were sealed'. Exact.
Asēr, Nephthalim, Manassē. Exact; note on Manasseh beside Joseph is accurate.
Zaboulōn, Iōsēph, Beniamin ... esphragismenoi. Exact. Irenaeus Haer. 5.30.2 on Dan and Jer 8:16 is correctly cited.

Re-parsed the hestōtes (nom.) / peribeblēmenous (acc.) irregularity and the resumptive auton; 'which no one could number', 'clothed in white robes, with palm branches' is exact and the irregularity is noted.
Hē sōtēria tō theō hēmōn ... kai tō arniō: verbless acclamation kept as 'Salvation to our God ... and to the Lamb!'. Defensible (ASV 'unto'); 'belongs to' is noted as the sense.
pantes hoi angeloi heistēkeisan kyklō tou thronou ... epesan ... epi ta prosōpa autōn kai prosekynēsan tō theō. Exact; 'four living creatures' matches 4:6-8.
Sevenfold doxology framed by Amēn; order eulogia, doxa, sophia, eucharistia, timē, dynamis, ischys preserved. dynamis 'power', ischys 'might'. Exact.
apekrithē ... legōn moi; Houtoi hoi peribeblēmenoi ... tines eisin kai pothen ēlthon. Exact; Septuagintal idiom noted.

eirēka autō; Kyrie mou, sy oidas; hoi erchomenoi ek tēs thlipseōs tēs megalēs; eplynan ... eleukanan ... en tō haimati tou arniou. Present participle kept; lower-case 'lord' for an address to the elder is correct.

skēnōsei ep' autous 'will spread his tabernacle over them' (ASV) keeps epi + accusative and the tabernacle noun-verb link; RSV's 'shelter them with his presence' is correctly labelled as interpretive. Disputed only against RSV/NRSV; the ASV wording is a defensible literal rendering.
ou peinasousin eti oude dipsēsousin eti, oude mē pesē ep' autous ho hēlios oude pan kauma. Exact; Isa 49:10 LXX allusion correct.

to arnion to ana meson tou thronou poimanei autous ... hodēgēsei autous epi zōēs pēgas hydatōn; exaleipsei ho theos pan dakryon. 'be their shepherd' is the pastoral sense the Isa 49:10 context requires; zōēs fronted is rendered 'springs of the waters of life'. Exact.

citations: LXX usage: kyrios for the Tetragrammaton, theos for ʾĕlōhîm
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct: theos never renders the Tetragrammaton in the LXX or NT, the canon's French reads 'Dieu' at every site, and published chapters 1, 4, 6 use 'God'. The canon's English 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' is recorded in reception notes without entering the line.

citations: BDAG s.vv. diabolos, Satanas, Abaddōn, Harmagedōn
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct for a presentation and scope convention. Recommendation (non-blocking): state the scope criterion explicitly. Hebrew-text central entries are applied to a Greek line when their English choice is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme (chayyot 'living creatures' at 7:11; gophrit 'sulfur' for theion). They are background only where applying them would import a Hebrew-specific form or sense (Yisra'el, 'the adversary', 'the deep'). Without that sentence the 7:11 chayyot ref and the gophrit extension look like exceptions to rule (4).

Direct is defensible: both senses are lexical and the context split (divine master vs free/slave pair) is the ASV/RSV/NRSV practice and the 1:1/6:15 precedent. The canon's French 'esclaves' is honestly recorded.
Direct is defensible: 'tabernacle' keeps the Lev 26/Ezek 37 allusion at 21:3, 'dwell' is universal for the verb, and the 7:15 ASV exception is grammatically motivated by epi + accusative.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 146 verses, the 10 overlay entries touched and the 13 diff ops were formed from the chapters, the SBLGNT sources (including the sigla-bearing Rev.txt in the scratchpad), the overlay, the diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-r2-editor-report.md. After reading the report, no verdict changed. The report's Founder point C lists the KJV-wording variants named in commentary (8:7, 9:13, 10:4, 21:2, 21:3 'his people ... their God', 21:4). It omits 21:3 'out of heaven', which confirms the reviewer's 21:3 revise. Its 9:13 request ('the Reviewer should verify this against the NA28 apparatus') was met as far as possible: the SBLGNT marker confirms a collated edition reads tessarōn, and the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger. The printed NA28 apparatus was not available, so this is recorded as unverified at the sigla level, not as a defect. The report's 'All other lines are the Translator's draft, unchanged' was confirmed by diffing against the rev_r2 backup: only 16:3 and 16:9 differ.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-theion-sulfur: Endorse. LXX theion = gophrit (Gen 19:24), BDAG 'sulfur', NRSV 'sulfur' at all four sites; the central entry already renders the Revelation lake passages 'sulfur'. The canon's English 'brimstone' (9:18) is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Complete the inventory: add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou) and 16:18 (NA28 singular; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'); correct 8:7 to say the omission is a TR reading, not the Byzantine majority's. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-names-and-scope-rule: Endorse, and support promotion to a central Greek-NT convention. Add the explicit criterion (apply where the central English is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme; background where it imports a Hebrew-specific form), which explains chayyot at 7:11 and gophrit for theion.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-exousia: Endorse. The context rule follows BDAG's sense division and RSV/NRSV practice; 16:9 'authority over' aligns with 6:8 and 13:7. Uniform 'authority' would read badly at 9:10, 19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-16:3-living-being: Endorse. 'soul' for sea creatures imports a personal sense; 'living being' keeps the noun and the nep̄eš ḥayyâ echo.
founderDecisionRecommendations.G-doulos-servants: Endorse. Keeps the signed-off 1:1/6:11 and the canon's English 'servants'; the French 'esclaves' is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.H-pit-of-the-abyss: Endorse. ASV structure; matches the canon's French 'le puits de l'abîme'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.I-Har-magedon: Endorse. ASV form, follows the SBLGNT/NA28 rough breathing, keeps har visible without deciding the etymology.
founderDecisionRecommendations.J-12:18-versification: Endorse. P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read estathē, and SBLGNT/NA28 number it 12:18 (Metzger on 12:18). The ASV 13:1a alignment is a tooling task (orchestrator follow-up 2), not a translation issue.

reviewerReport.summary: 17 verdicts: 17 approve. No revise or flag. Reception note at 7:3 verified.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἶδον τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὰς τέσσαρας γωνίας τῆς γῆς, κρατοῦντας τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀνέμους τῆς γῆς, ἵνα μὴ πνέῃ ἄνεμος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μήτε ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης μήτε ἐπὶ πᾶν δένδρον.
paragraphs.translit: meta touto eidon tessaras angelous hestōtas epi tas tessaras gōnias tēs gēs, kratountas tous tessaras anemous tēs gēs, hina mē pneē anemos epi tēs gēs mēte epi tēs thalassēs mēte epi pan dendron.

i18n.en: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back the four winds of the earth, so that no wind should blow on the earth or on the sea or upon any tree.

notes.official: *Meta touto eidon* 'After this I saw' opens the interlude between the sixth and seventh seals (7:1-17). *epi tas tessaras gōnias tēs gēs* 'at the four corners of the earth' and *tous tessaras anemous tēs gēs* 'the four winds of the earth' are the standard biblical figures for the whole earth (Isa 11:12; Ezek 7:2; Jer 49:36; Zech 6:5; Dan 7:2). Winds as agents of destruction, held back until the servants are sealed, recall Jer 49:36 and the wind-gates of 1 En 76, collected in the central `twelve-gates-four-winds-cosmography-1-enoch-76-cross-corpus` and `four-corners-gates-of-heaven-1-enoch-33-36-cosmic-geography-cross-corpus` (background, not applied). The line is literal (ASV).

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἀναβαίνοντα ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου, ἔχοντα σφραγῖδα θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τοῖς τέσσαρσιν ἀγγέλοις οἷς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἀδικῆσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon allon angelon anabainonta apo anatolēs hēliou, echonta sphragida theou zōntos, kai ekraxen phōnē megalē tois tessarsin angelois hois edothē autois adikēsai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan,

i18n.en: And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it had been given to harm the earth and the sea,

notes.official: *apo anatolēs hēliou* 'from the rising of the sun', i.e. from the east (ASV 'from the sunrising'). *sphragida theou zōntos* 'the seal of the living God': a seal ring or stamp, the instrument that marks ownership and protects; *theos zōn* 'the living God' is Septuagintal (Deut 5:26; Hos 2:1 LXX). *hois edothē autois adikēsai* 'to whom it had been given to harm': the pronoun *autois* resumes the relative, a Semitism frequent in Revelation (Charles, ICC; Aune, WBC 52B), which English cannot reproduce. *theos* is 'God' throughout (`theos-god-rendering-against-canon-english-yahweh-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: λέγων· Μὴ ἀδικήσητε τὴν γῆν μήτε τὴν θάλασσαν μήτε τὰ δένδρα, ἄχρι σφραγίσωμεν τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· mē adikēsēte tēn gēn mēte tēn thalassan mēte ta dendra, achri sphragisōmen tous doulous tou theou hēmōn epi tōn metōpōn autōn.

i18n.en: saying: "Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads."

notes.official:
*achri sphragisōmen tous doulous tou theou hēmōn epi tōn metōpōn autōn* 'until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads'. The model is Ezek 9:4-6, where a man clothed in linen marks a *tāw* on the foreheads of those who grieve over Jerusalem's abominations, and they are spared. The mark returns as the name of the Lamb and of the Father on the foreheads of the 144,000 (14:1; 22:4), and the beast's mark parodies it (13:16). The forehead-name tradition is collected in the central `seal-on-forehead-name-of-yhwh-cross-corpus-shiur-qomah-ezekiel-9-revelation-14-22` (background). *doulos* is 'servant' where God or Christ is the master and 'slave' in the social pair free/slave (`doulos-servant-slave-rendering-revelation`; 13:16; 6:15).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 2-3 (French 'les esclaves de notre Dieu', English edition 'the servants of our God') and reads those 'sealed in the forehead' as the people whose cellular plan is transmitted by manual contact with the forehead bone, about 144,000 in all (cf. v 4). The line keeps the lexical 'sealed' and 'servants' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐσφραγισμένων, ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, ἐσφραγισμένοι ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa ton arithmon tōn esphragismenōn, hekaton tesserakonta tessares chiliades, esphragismenoi ek pasēs phylēs huiōn israēl·

i18n.en: And I heard the number of those who were sealed, a hundred and forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the sons of Israel:

notes.official: *hekaton tesserakonta tessares chiliades* '144,000' is 12 × 12 × 1,000, a number built on the tribal twelve. *ek pasēs phylēs huiōn Israēl* 'out of every tribe of the sons of Israel': *huioi Israēl* is the Septuagint calque of *bənê yiśrāʾēl* (ASV 'the children of Israel'), and 'sons' keeps the Greek. Names are given in their standard English forms, as everywhere in the Greek books of the corpus. The central `shivtei-yisrael-shenim-asar-twelve-tribes-institutional-political-formula-cross-corpus` ('the twelve tribes of Yisra'el') names Rev 7:5-8 as a reception site, but it governs the Hebrew text and is not applied to a Greek line (`greek-nt-proper-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι, ἐκ φυλῆς Ῥουβὴν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Γὰδ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
paragraphs.translit: ek phylēs iouda dōdeka chiliades esphragismenoi, ek phylēs rhoubēn dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs gad dōdeka chiliades,

i18n.en: from the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed, from the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, from the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,

notes.official: The list (vv 5-8) opens with Judah, not with Reuben the firstborn; most commentators connect this with the messianic tribe (Gen 49:10; Rev 5:5 'the Lion of the tribe of Judah'). The Greek forms are *Iouda*, *Rhoubēn*, *Gad*. *esphragismenoi* 'were sealed' frames the list here and at v 8.

paragraphs.text: ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσὴρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Νεφθαλὶμ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Μανασσῆ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
paragraphs.translit: ek phylēs asēr dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs nephthalim dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs manassē dōdeka chiliades,

i18n.en: from the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, from the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand, from the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand,

notes.official: *Nephthalim* is the Septuagint form of Naphtali. Manasseh is listed alongside Joseph (v 8), although Manasseh is itself one of the two Joseph tribes; with Dan absent, the count still comes to twelve.

paragraphs.text: ἐκ φυλῆς Συμεὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Λευὶ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰσσαχὰρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
paragraphs.translit: ek phylēs symeōn dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs leui dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs issachar dōdeka chiliades,

i18n.en: from the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand, from the tribe of Levi twelve thousand, from the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand,

notes.official: Levi, the priestly tribe that has no territory in most tribal lists of the Hebrew Bible (Num 1:47-49; Josh 13:14), is counted here as a tribe like the others.

paragraphs.text: ἐκ φυλῆς Ζαβουλὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰωσὴφ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι.
paragraphs.translit: ek phylēs zaboulōn dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs iōsēph dōdeka chiliades, ek phylēs beniamin dōdeka chiliades esphragismenoi.

i18n.en: from the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, from the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, from the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.

notes.official: Dan and Ephraim are absent, and Joseph stands where Ephraim would be expected. The earliest explanation of Dan's omission is Irenaeus (*Haer.* 5.30.2), who reads Jer 8:16 LXX as foretelling that the Antichrist would come from Dan; modern commentators also point to Dan's association with idolatry (Judg 18; 1 Kgs 12:29-30) (Aune, WBC 52B; Bauckham, *The Climax of Prophecy*, 1993). The list matches none of the tribal lists of the Hebrew Bible, and the line reproduces it as it stands.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ὄχλος πολύς, ὃν ἀριθμῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο, ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνους καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν, ἑστῶτες ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου, περιβεβλημένους στολὰς λευκάς, καὶ φοίνικες ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: meta tauta eidon, kai idou ochlos polys, hon arithmēsai auton oudeis edynato, ek pantos ethnous kai phylōn kai laōn kai glōssōn, hestōtes enōpion tou thronou kai enōpion tou arniou, peribeblēmenous stolas leukas, kai phoinikes en tais chersin autōn·

i18n.en: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude, which no one could number, from every nation and from all tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands;

notes.official: *ochlos polys, hon arithmēsai auton oudeis edynato* 'a great multitude, which no one could number': the resumptive *auton* is again Semitic. The fourfold 'nation, tribes, peoples, tongues' (cf. Dan 3:4; 7:14) recurs in varying order at 10:11 and 13:7. The shift from nominative *hestōtes* 'standing' to accusative *peribeblēmenous* 'clothed' is one of the book's characteristic irregularities, which English cannot show. *phoinikes* 'palm branches', as at the feast of Booths (Lev 23:40) and the entry into Jerusalem (John 12:13).

paragraphs.text: καὶ κράζουσι φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἡ σωτηρία τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai krazousi phōnē megalē legontes· hē sōtēria tō theō hēmōn tō kathēmenō epi tō thronō kai tō arniō.

i18n.en: and they cry out with a loud voice, saying: "Salvation to our God who is seated on the throne, and to the Lamb!"

notes.official: *Hē sōtēria tō theō hēmōn ... kai tō arniō* 'Salvation to our God ... and to the Lamb!': a verbless acclamation ascribing the deliverance to God and the Lamb ('salvation belongs to'); the line keeps the acclamatory form without supplying a verb (ASV 'Salvation unto our God').

paragraphs.text: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι εἱστήκεισαν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων, καὶ ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ,
paragraphs.translit: kai pantes hoi angeloi heistēkeisan kyklō tou thronou kai tōn presbyterōn kai tōn tessarōn zōōn, kai epesan enōpion tou thronou epi ta prosōpa autōn kai prosekynēsan tō theō,

i18n.en: And all the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God,

notes.official: *tōn tessarōn zōōn* 'the four living creatures' of 4:6-8 (`four-living-creatures-rev-4-6-8-ezek-1-chayyot-shiur-qomah-cross-corpus`; `chayyot`). *prosekynēsan* 'worshiped' denotes prostration, made explicit by 'fell on their faces'.

paragraphs.text: λέγοντες· Ἀμήν· ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ εὐχαριστία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: legontes· amēn· hē eulogia kai hē doxa kai hē sophia kai hē eucharistia kai hē timē kai hē dynamis kai hē ischys tō theō hēmōn eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn· amēn.

i18n.en: saying: "Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might be to our God forever and ever. Amen."

notes.official: A sevenfold doxology framed by *Amēn*. It matches the sevenfold doxology to the Lamb at 5:12, with *eucharistia* 'thanksgiving' in place of *ploutos* 'riches'. *dynamis* 'power' and *ischys* 'might' (see `exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation` for the distinction from *exousia*).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγων μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ περιβεβλημένοι τὰς στολὰς τὰς λευκὰς τίνες εἰσὶν καὶ πόθεν ἦλθον;
paragraphs.translit: kai apekrithē heis ek tōn presbyterōn legōn moi· houtoi hoi peribeblēmenoi tas stolas tas leukas tines eisin kai pothen ēlthon;

i18n.en: And one of the elders answered, saying to me: "These who are clothed in the white robes, who are they, and where have they come from?"

notes.official: *apekrithē ... legōn* 'answered, saying': the Septuagintal idiom (Heb. *wayyaʿan ... wayyōʾmer*), used even when no question has been asked. The elder acts as the interpreting angel of Zech 1-6 and Dan 7-8, asking the question in order to answer it.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἴρηκα αὐτῷ· Κύριέ μου, σὺ οἶδας. καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι ἐκ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἔπλυναν τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλεύκαναν αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ἀρνίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai eirēka autō· kyrie mou, sy oidas. kai eipen moi· houtoi eisin hoi erchomenoi ek tēs thlipseōs tēs megalēs, kai eplynan tas stolas autōn kai eleukanan autas en tō haimati tou arniou.

i18n.en: And I said to him: "My lord, you know." And he said to me: "These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

notes.official: *Kyrie mou* 'My lord': a respectful address to the elder, not a divine title, so lower case. *eirēka* 'I said' is a perfect used as a narrative tense. *hoi erchomenoi ek tēs thlipseōs tēs megalēs* 'the ones who come out of the great tribulation': the present participle is kept; 'the great tribulation' draws on Dan 12:1 (Th *thlipsis*). Robes made white in blood is a deliberate paradox, built on Gen 49:11 and Isa 1:18. The elder's speech runs to v 17.

paragraphs.text: διὰ τοῦτό εἰσιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ λατρεύουσιν αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου σκηνώσει ἐπʼ αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto eisin enōpion tou thronou tou theou, kai latreuousin autō hēmeras kai nyktos en tō naō autou, kai ho kathēmenos epi tou thronou skēnōsei epʼ autous.

i18n.en: Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple; and the one seated on the throne will spread his tabernacle over them.

notes.official: *skēnōsei ep' autous* 'will spread his tabernacle over them'. *skēnoō* 'pitch a tent, dwell' is the verb of *skēnē*, the Septuagint word for the tabernacle (*miškān*), and the Greek counterpart of Heb. *šāḵan* (central `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`, background). With *epi* 'over' the image is the divine presence spread like a canopy over the people, as the cloud and fire over Zion in Isa 4:5-6 (cf. Ezek 37:27). The ASV wording keeps both the tabernacle and the covering; RSV 'shelter them with his presence' interprets the image (`skene-skenoo-tabernacle-dwell-rendering-revelation`). *latreuousin* 'they serve' is cultic service, and *naos* 'temple' is the sanctuary proper.

paragraphs.text: οὐ πεινάσουσιν ἔτι οὐδὲ διψήσουσιν ἔτι, οὐδὲ μὴ πέσῃ ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὁ ἥλιος οὐδὲ πᾶν καῦμα,
paragraphs.translit: ou peinasousin eti oude dipsēsousin eti, oude mē pesē epʼ autous ho hēlios oude pan kauma,

i18n.en: They will hunger no more, nor thirst any more; nor will the sun strike them, nor any scorching heat,

notes.official: Isa 49:10, close to the Septuagint: 'they shall not hunger nor thirst, nor shall the scorching heat (*kausōn*) nor the sun strike them'. *oude mē pesē ep' autous* 'nor will ... strike them' (literally 'fall upon them') is the emphatic negation with *ou mē*.

paragraphs.text: ὅτι τὸ ἀρνίον τὸ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ θρόνου ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς, καὶ ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐξαλείψει ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti to arnion to ana meson tou thronou poimanei autous, kai hodēgēsei autous epi zōēs pēgas hydatōn· kai exaleipsei ho theos pan dakryon ek tōn ophthalmōn autōn.

i18n.en: for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will be their shepherd, and will guide them to springs of the waters of life; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes."

notes.official: *to arnion to ana meson tou thronou* 'the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne' (5:6). *poimanei autous* 'will be their shepherd': *poimainō* has its pastoral sense here, supported by the continuation of Isa 49:10 ('he who has mercy on them will lead them, and by springs of water will guide them'); at 12:5, in the quotation of Ps 2:9, the same verb is 'rule'. *zōēs pēgas hydatōn* 'springs of the waters of life': *zōēs* stands first for emphasis (ASV 'fountains of waters of life'). *exaleipsei ho theos pan dakryon* 'God will wipe away every tear' quotes Isa 25:8 and returns at 21:4. The elder's speech closes here.
